messages.content: Write a post about why a company is investing in developer relations. Around 250 words.

output:
**Why we're funding devrel**

We're hiring three people into developer relations this quarter. Devrel is usually the first line cut in a tight year, so here's the argument we made internally.

In March we read every support ticket filed in a user's first week. Just over half were questions the docs never answered — not bugs, not outages, just people stuck on the shape of the thing. Each one cost us a support engineer's afternoon and, more often than we'd like to admit, the account. You can't patch that with a status page.

The other half of the argument is slower and harder to put on a slide. The people who choose our API are rarely the people who sign the contract. They try it on a Saturday, hit a wall or don't, and six months later someone in procurement calls us. By then the decision is already made. Everything that happens on that Saturday — the quickstart, the error message, whether an actual engineer answers the GitHub issue — is the sale.

So devrel here isn't a marketing function and won't report into marketing. It reports to engineering, owns the docs, and has a standing mandate to file bugs against our own product when the tutorial gets embarrassing.

What we'll measure: time from signup to first successful API call, and how many first-week tickets we stop getting. If those two numbers don't move by January, we were wrong and we'll say so.

Questions welcome. We'll post the job descriptions Thursday.
